chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ta'i narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Khashab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Muhsin narrated to us from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father (peace be upon them all). He said:

Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: By Allah, your world means nothing to me except like the spit in the mouth of one who grasps a locust and then throws it out. What benefit is there in a blessing that passes away or a property that will be seized? O people, this world is a passing abode, not a permanent dwelling. Its people are of two types: the one who sold himself [for it] and destroyed himself, and the one who purchased himself and freed himself. What has perished of it is not hoped for in return, and what remains of it is not known as lasting. Its joy turns to sorrow, its sorrow is not repelled, its good is blotted out, and its evil cannot be turned away.

(Quran 11:15-16) 'Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments — We fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein. Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire. And lost is what they did therein, and worthless is what they used to do.'

How can I endure the Fire when you could not bear the heated iron rod even for the sake of a game? How then can I be patient with a fire kindled by God's wrath? You flee from the pain of a needle, so how would you endure its scorpions, its irons, and its flames? By Allah, I have heard that a man from the inhabitants of al-Mada'in followed after the Hanifiyya (Islam) and donned its trappings and then abandoned it for the religion of the Zoroastrians, riding their horses and adopting their customs. May Allah fight him! He sold the part of the eternal, vast, abundant kingdom for the part of the perishable, meager, narrow world.

O my Shia community, beware! The world has warned you with its fangs, snatching souls one after another like a wolf among a flock of scattered sheep. By Allah, I see how your Imam obeys Allah while you disobey. Your enemies transgress against Allah and you hold back. Those who love you are harmed for your sake while those who hate you are honoured on your account. By Allah, if you were struck with a sword in Allah's cause, it would be better for you than meeting Him with something that corrupts your religion.

I have received word that a man from the inhabitants of al-Mada'in followed after the Hanifiyya and adopted their ways, wearing their garments and living by their customs, until his death came to him in that state. Woe to him! He traded the eternal for the perishable. I indeed met a group from the people of this world who marvel at those who are satisfied with what Allah has given them, and who deride those who eat dry bread with a trace of salt. Yet by Allah, if I wished I could order honey mixed with the finest wheat and the best meat — but how far away is that from my desire! How can one whose resolution is not reached except after great hardship know what I mean? And how can one engrossed in comfort understand the delight of those striving in the way of Allah?

By Allah, I have seen my brother Aqil fallen into poverty to the point that he begged from me a measure of your grain, and returned to me asking for ten camel-loads of your barley to feed his hungry children, whose disheveled faces had contracted from the cold of their suffering. He returned and repeated his request. I leaned my ear toward him and it deceived him — he thought I would yield my religion and follow what pleases him. So I heated an iron rod for him so that he might desist, since he could neither approach it nor bear it. Then I brought it near his body and he screamed from its pain like one gravely ill moaning from his sickness. He nearly cursed me in his suppressed anguish. Then I said to him: 'May the bereaved women mourn you, O Aqil! Do you moan from a rod heated by a human being as a game, yet you drag me toward a fire ignited by its All-Compeller out of His wrath? Do you moan from the pain and I do not moan from the blazing fire of Hell?'

By Allah, if accountability were removed from the nations and they were left in their graves, rotting in their bones, I would still be ashamed before the contempt of an Ever-Watchful Observer who exposes shameful deeds and sins that are recorded. So be patient with a world that passes with its tribulations like a night passes with its dreams. How great is the distance between a soul at ease in its tents and a sinner in Hellfire screaming! And do not be amazed by this — rather be amazed at the visitor who came to us without any contrivance on our part, with wrapped food and a sweet confection. I said to him: 'Is this charity, a vow, or zakat? All of that is forbidden to us, the People of the House of Prophethood; and its replacement is the one-fifth (khums) of those with close kinship in the Book and Sunnah.' He said to me: 'No, it is neither — it is a gift.' So I said: 'May the bereaved women mourn you! Are you trying to trick me away from the religion of Allah with a confection drowned in your sugar and a yellow sweetmeat brought to me with the juice of your dates? Are you confused or possessed? Are not the souls accountable for the weight of a mustard seed? What then shall I say about a confection I would be forced to swallow, especially one prepared in such a way?'

O Allah, I have fled from it with the flight of a filly from its rider. I show him the small stars and he shows me the moon. Do I refuse a strand of camel hair from a young she-camel that has fallen, yet swallow camels in their resting place, their scorpions crawling from their nests, deadly spotted snakes in my sleeping chamber? So leave me. Let me be satisfied with your world with my salt and my loaves of bread. For with the fear of Allah I hope for my salvation. What does Ali have to do with a perishing pleasure or a delight born of sins? I shall meet my Lord and my Shia with bitter weeping eyes and empty stomachs.
(Quran 3:141) 'That Allah may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers.' And we seek refuge in Allah from the evil of deeds.

key_terms.أَهْلُ بَيْتِ النُّبُوَّةِ: The People of the House of Prophethood — the Ahl al-Bayt, forbidden from receiving zakat and sadaqa
key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: Al-dunya — the present world, depicted as transient, vile, and dangerous
key_terms.الزُّهْد: Zuhd — asceticism, renunciation of the world's pleasures for the sake of the Hereafter
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: Khums — the one-fifth tax mandated for the near of kin in the Quran (8:41), the divinely ordained compensation for the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.تَقْوَى: Taqwa — God-wariness, piety; cited as the Imam's sole hope for salvation
key_terms.ثَكِلَتْكَ الثَّوَاكِلُ: A classical Arabic curse/expression of strong rebuke: 'May the bereaved women mourn you'
key_terms.لَظَى: Laza — a Quranic name for the blazing fire of Hell (Quran 70:15)
key_terms.مَعَاشِرَ شِيعَتِي: O my Shia — direct address to the Shia community, a hallmark of Alid exhortatory discourse

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the world and asceticism in the sermon of Al-Amali of Saduq?
ai.summary: This is a famous sermon of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), transmitted through the chain of the Imams down to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq. Delivered in the spirit of zuhd (asceticism), it expresses the Imam's profound indifference to the world's pleasures through powerful rhetorical imagery — comparing worldly delights to poison, fire, and bitter colocynth. The sermon includes the famous story of Aqil's request for extra stipend and Imam Ali's response with a heated iron rod, illustrating that the Imam would sooner endure physical hardship than compromise divine justice. It concludes with a declaration that he and his Shia will meet Allah with eyes weeping and bellies empty — purified through voluntary abstinence.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa al-Daqqaq (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Ta'i narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn al-Khashab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Muhsin narrated to us from al-Mufaddal b. `Umar from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his grandfather from his father (as). He said:

Amir al-Mu’minin `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) said: By Allah, your world is nothing to me but a journey over a sweet waterfall: when the captain shouts out to them, they abandon ship. In my eye, its delight is like drinking scalding water and pus. It is a gulp of bitter, toxic water. It is snake poison. It is a bottomless cup. It is a strangling necklace of fire. I have repaired my armour until I felt shame from the one who repairs it, and he said to me: “hoist it off as a donkey hoists [its rider].” So, I said: “Get away from me”, for in the morning, the people praise the night, and the remanent of drowsiness passes. Had I wished, I would have robed myself in rugs embroidered with brocade, I would have eaten the kernels of the Earth with chicken breasts, and I would have drunk clear water with the thinnest of your glasses. However, I trust Allah when He says,

“Those who desire the life of the present and its glitter, to them we shall pay (the price of) their deeds therein – without diminution. They are those for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire: vain are the designs they frame therein, and of no effect and the deeds that they do!” (11:15-16)

So, how can I be patient on a fire, for if a spark of which was to be dislodged on earth, it would burn its vegetation; and even if a pea were to be secured, then this fire would ripen it? And which is better for `Ali: for him to be close to the Owner of the Throne, or to be in flames, lowly, banished, resented for his crime, lying? By Allah, to sleep on thorns as a bed, with my clothes were beneath me, laid onto the mix of dust and thorns; or to be dragged while shackled in my chains is more beloved to me than meeting Muhammad on the Day of Reckoning having betrayed an orphan, and oppressing him with his money intentionally – and I have never oppressed the orphan nor the non-orphan! A soul hastening its travel to its trials,  And its parts spread under the depths of the Earth,  And even if it was to live very long,  Then it would still dismount in proximity to the Owner of the Throne.

My Shi`a! Beware, for this world has bitten you with its canines, grabbing soul after soul, just like its wolves, and the camels of departure have been prepared for their riders. Surely, this conversation has intersecting branches, so none of you should say that the speech of `Ali is contradictory, for this talk is interdependent.

It has reached me that a man from the residents of Mada’in has followed, after being on the upright religion (al-Hanifiyya), the disbelieving mercenaries, and worn the sewn gifts of his town‘s political head, and perfumed himself with the musk of these containers in the morning, and wears the incense of India when he leaves, and he smells the aroma of the flowers of the garden around him, and the cushions of the Romans have been spread on his bead. Woe to him! After he has reached seventy years of age, and around him is an old man on the ground due to his old age, and an orphan aching from aggravation and from the desire to taste meat, he did not even console them with the surplus of his sweet blessings.  If Allah gives me power over him, then I would antagonize him the antagonization of an upright person, and I would apply the penalty (hadd) on him twice, and I would strike him eighty times after carrying the penalty, and I would not give him an excuse for his ignorance. Woe to him! Does he not feel? [Does he not wear] clothing of wool, clothing of hair? [Does he not eat] plain bread? Does he not feed one in need at night? Does a tear on his cheek not roll at night? If he was a believer, then his matters in what he does not own would be organized.

By Allah, I have seen `Aqil, my brother, impoverished, until he requested from the small measure of ḥis grain weighing device, and then he returned asking for an exorbitant measure of your barley to feed his hungry ones, and he almost went on his third famishing day, and I saw his children, their colours matted from the suffering, as if their faces have been severely changed from the cold. When he returned and repeated his speech, I listened to him so it piqued his interest, and thought I would corrupt my religion and follow what pleases him, so I heated a piece of iron to rebuke him, because he cannot get near it or be patient on its heat. Then, I brought it near to his body, so he shouted from his pain, the shouting of an extremely ill person moaning from his illness. He almost insulted me wrongfully due to his suppression, and the burning of the flaming heat of illness caused from his impoverishment, so I said to him: “May the mourners mourn you, `Aq̣il. Do you moan from an iron playfully heated by a human, and drag me to a Fire angrily ignited its Compeller? Do you moan from the pain, and I don’t moan from the flames [of Hell]?

By Allah, if reward was to be lifted from nations, and they were to be left in their graves as weak bones, would I feel embarrassed from the spite of an Observer, who exposed hidden wicked actions which can be abrogated? So, patience on a world whose hardships pass like a night and its dreams. How many a soul sleeping soundly in its pavilion, and a sinner screaming in hellfire? And do not be surprised by this, but be surprised by what we have been tested with, from a person who knocked with folded [food] in plates, and a Ma`jūna (sweet) laid in bowls. So, I said to him: “Is this a donation? Or nithr? Or zakat? All of that is forbidden for us, the Household of Prophethood, and we have been given in its place the khums of the close of kin in the Book and Sunna.” So, he said to me: “No this, nor that, but it is a gift.” So, I said to him: “May the mourners mourn you! Do you trick me away from the religion of Allah with a Ma`juna dipped in your sugar, and a yellow Khabisa (sweet) you’ve brought to me with the juice of your dates? Are you confused, crazy, or insane? Aren’t the souls asked about even the amount of a mustard  seed? So, what about a prepared Ma`jūuna that I bitterly eat?” By Allah, if I was given the seven pens, with all the universes under it, and all its inhabitants would obey me, giving me all their possession, with the cost of disobeying Allah by robbing a grain of barley from an ant for me to chew, then I would not accept and would not want. Your world to me is more lowly than a leaf crushed by the teeth of a grasshopper, and dirtier to me than the bones eaten by a pig which spits the chewed remanent, and is more bitter to my heart than the desert gourd chewed by an ill person to the point that he gets tired of it. So, how can I accept the things strongly folded inside it, kneaded with the saliva or pus of a snake?

O Allah! I have fled from it the fleeing of a female horse from the one who rides it. “I show him the night and he shows me the moon (missing the obvious)” Do I give up the fallen hair of a female camel, and give up tied horses in their parking place? Do I catch cyclones of scorpions in their den, or do I tie the killer snakes on my bed? So, let me be sufficed from your world with my salt and loaves, for with God-wariness, I beg for my salvation. What is for `Ali and a perishing blessing, and sweetness produced from sins? I shall, alongside my Shi`a, meet Our Lord with bitter eyes and empty stomachs,
“that Allah may purify the believers [through trial] and destroy the disbelievers” [3:141]; and we seek refuge om Allah from wicked actions.
